clue.text: Footwork of judoka caught in video recording

indicators.note: the judoka and the catch sit inside the recording, so 'in' places them within it

parts.note: a tape is a video recording
a dan is a grade of judo black belt, so a judoka can be one
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A martial-arts move by a judo fighter is captured on camera.
explanation.walkthrough: DAN, a judo grade, stands for the judoka; with C it goes inside TAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tap dancing is a dance form built entirely on rhythmic footwork, so the phrase describes it.

clue.text: Way to get irrational number's root

parts.note: a turn is a way of doing something or a bend in a road

indicators.note: irrational suggests disorder, so the letters of the number are scrambled

parts.note: pi is the famous irrational number

explanation.surface: A mathematical method for finding the square root of an irrational number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'root' looks mathematical but is the vegetable; 'irrational' scrambles PI into IP.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnip is a root vegetable, eaten for its swollen underground part.

clue.text: Opium taken regularly by posh person as an excuse …

indicators.note: taken regularly picks out every other letter of the word

parts.note: a toff is British slang for an upper-class person

explanation.surface: A posh drug-taker uses opium as a pretext for something.
explanation.walkthrough: TOFF is British slang for an upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: A put-off is an evasive reply or pretext for delay, which is an excuse.

clue.text: … to pass out as part of a posh farewell

indicators.note: as part of puts the dying inside the other letters

parts.note: U means upper class, as in U and non-U
to pass out can mean to pass away, to die

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, the posh person faints during a grand goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 2 Down; DIE sits inside A U, where U is the old label for upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is the French goodbye used in English, a formal farewell.

clue.text: Queen's daughter left after first half of Chas & Dave?

indicators.note: after places the princess and left behind the half word
first half of takes the opening two of the four letters

parts.note: Princess Anne is the late Queen Elizabeth II's daughter

explanation.surface: A royal joins the cockney duo Chas & Dave, half way through.
explanation.walkthrough: Chas & Dave were a London pop duo, but 'Dave' alone is the definition: Dave is a British TV channel, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Dave is a UK television station known for comedy repeats, an example of a broadcasting service.

clue.text: Intro of Suspicious Minds is shocking

indicators.note: the intro of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of Suspicious is used

parts.note: to mind is to care, so minds means cares

explanation.surface: The opening of Elvis's song Suspicious Minds is said to be startling.
explanation.walkthrough: Suspicious Minds is an Elvis Presley song, but here the words are split: S from the first and CARES from the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that scares a person frightens or alarms them, which is what shocking means.

clue.text: Eat, in or out — see you shortly outside for a drink

indicators.note: outside means the text-speak letters wrap round the rest

parts.note: CU is text-speak shorthand for see you

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone decides whether to dine in or out, then meets a friend for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges EAT IN OR into OINTREA, which C and U then wrap round.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is a French orange-flavoured liqueur, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: One from Latvia interrupting Uruguay-Spain game

indicators.note: interrupting means the Latvian breaks into the middle of the other letters

parts.note: ROU is the international vehicle code for Uruguay
E is the international vehicle code for Spain
a Lett is a native of Latvia

explanation.surface: A Latvian player disrupts a football match between Uruguay and Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Roulette is a casino gambling game played with a spinning wheel and ball.

clue.text: Female with doctorate to cuddle Queen's Guide

parts.note: she is the female pronoun

indicators.note: to cuddle is to hold close, so the doctorate wraps round the royal letters

parts.note: PhD is the doctor of philosophy degree
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A woman with a doctorate hugs the Queen's Girl Guide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guide' looks like a Girl Guide noun but is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To shepherd people is to guide them along, as a herder leads a flock.

clue.text: Dramatic art giant?

indicators.note: dramatic suggests a theatrical upheaval, telling us to rearrange the letters that follow

explanation.surface: A towering figure of the theatre is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: 'Dramatic' rearranges ART GIANT, and the clue describes the playwright Terence Rattigan, author of The Browning Version.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence Rattigan was a major twentieth-century English playwright, a giant of the dramatic arts.

clue.text: Thin cover put around pick-up truck

indicators.note: put around means the word for cover is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: a lid is a cover
a ute is an Australian name for a pick-up truck

explanation.surface: A flimsy tarpaulin is wrapped round a pick-up truck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thin' is a verb here, not the adjective the surface suggests; 'put around' reverses the cover word. A ute is the Australian name for a pick-up.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilute a liquid is to thin it by adding water, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: English playwright, male, not welcome in all-female area

indicators.note: not welcome means the male is shut out of the word

parts.note: a harem is the women's quarters of a household

explanation.surface: A male dramatist is unwelcome in a space reserved for women.
explanation.definitionFit: David Hare is an English dramatist, author of Plenty and Skylight.

clue.text: South Africa to override the Church in power? It makes me sick

indicators.note: to override is to take the place of, so one set of letters displaces another

parts.note: influence is power over others
CE stands for the Church of England
ZA is the international code for South Africa

explanation.surface: A political protest about South African interference with the Church makes the speaker feel ill.
explanation.walkthrough: In INFLUENCE the final CE (Church of England) is replaced by ZA.
explanation.definitionFit: Flu is an illness, so the virus is something that makes a person sick.

clue.text: Support most of the ones like Tusk?

parts.note: a tee is the peg that supports a golf ball

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: A question about backing a politician like Donald Tusk.
explanation.walkthrough: Tusk looks like the Polish politician Donald Tusk; with a lower-case reading, a tusk is a long tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: A tusk is an elongated tooth, so tusks are examples of these.

clue.text: Register a car of superior quality but not special

indicators.note: but not tells us to leave out the following letter

parts.note: a Rolls, short for Rolls-Royce, is the byword for a luxury car

explanation.surface: Someone registers a luxury car that is ordinary rather than special.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll is an official list of names, such as an electoral register.

clue.text: A great loss nearly spoilt Freud's early childhood

indicators.note: spoilt means damaged out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
nearly means the word is cut short by its final letter

explanation.surface: A major bereavement nearly ruined a childhood, as Freud might analyse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' trims LOSS to LOS, and 'spoilt' rearranges A GREAT LOS.
explanation.definitionFit: In Freudian theory the oral stage is the first phase of psychosexual development, in infancy.

clue.text: Sportsperson held hostage by eleven terrorists

indicators.note: the letters are held captive inside the words that follow, which signals a concealed word

explanation.surface: An athlete is taken captive by a group of eleven terrorists.
explanation.definitionFit: An eventer competes in equestrian eventing, so the rider is a kind of sportsperson.

clue.text: Small group of farmers entering my land, sacking and jeering

indicators.note: entering means the farmers go inside the other letters

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!

indicators.note: sacking means getting rid of, so the second word is thrown out of the first

parts.note: the NFU is Britain's National Farmers' Union

explanation.surface: Farmers trespass on someone's land, ransacking and mocking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacking' removes AND from LAND, leaving L; S, COR and L then take in NFU, the National Farmers' Union.
explanation.definitionFit: Scornful behaviour shows contempt, as jeering mockery does.

clue.text: Strong man accepted universal credit: "just right to accept it"

parts.note: A is a recognised abbreviation for accepted, as on a bill
U is the film-classification abbreviation for universal

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so the phrase holds the credit

parts.note: to a T means exactly or just right
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A tough guy claims his welfare payment, Universal Credit, is fair and proper.
explanation.walkthrough: Universal Credit is a British welfare benefit, but here the two words are split; 'to a T' means exactly right.
explanation.definitionFit: An autocrat rules with absolute power, a strongman leader.

clue.text: Bottle about as old as we are

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
of the same age as us is our age

explanation.surface: A wine bottle is said to be roughly the same vintage as the speakers.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottle is British slang for nerve or bravery, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle in British slang means nerve, the boldness to face danger.

clue.text: Motörhead legend heading off for award

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: Lemmy Kilmister was the founding frontman of Motörhead

explanation.surface: The Motörhead frontman leaves to collect a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: An Emmy is an American television prize.

clue.text: Right from the start Brexit looked utterly exciting

indicators.note: from the start asks for the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Someone claims Brexit seemed thrilling right from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative Party, so it stands for the political right.
explanation.definitionFit: In British politics the Conservatives' colour is blue, so the word denotes the right wing.

clue.text: Black Friday's ending — grabbing special treat will cause bodily harm

indicators.note: grabbing means the outer letters clutch the rest

parts.note: B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

indicators.note: ending picks out the closing letter of the day's name
special here means made unusual, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Black Friday shoppers fight over a bargain, causing injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' rearranges TREAT into ATTER, which B and Y, the end of Friday, hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Battery is the legal term for unlawful physical force against a person, as in assault and battery.

clue.text: Tory admits to endlessly ponder over newspaper article

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the party letters hold the rest

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the Tory party

indicators.note: over means the trimmed word is turned round
endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to mull something over is to ponder it

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician confesses to brooding over a newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims MULL to MUL, and 'over' turns it to LUM, which CON admits.
explanation.definitionFit: A column is a regular feature written by one journalist in a newspaper.

clue.text: Fruit & Fibre artist exchanged for hard drugs

indicators.note: exchanged for means one set of letters is swapped out for another

parts.note: Lycra is a stretchy synthetic fibre
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
E is slang for ecstasy, so two Es are drugs

explanation.surface: Reads like the breakfast cereal Fruit 'n Fibre, with an artist trading it for drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Fruit 'n Fibre is a British breakfast cereal, but the words split: Fruit is the definition and Fibre gives LYCRA.
explanation.definitionFit: The lychee is a sweet Asian fruit with a rough red skin.

clue.text: Origins of Android not British

indicators.note: not means the letter for British is left out

parts.note: an android is a humanlike robot, here taken in the plural

explanation.surface: The beginnings of the Android phone system are said not to be British.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Android' looks like the phone software; here it is a robot, and the definition, 'Origins', is plural, so ROBOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Roots are the sources from which something grows, so the word means origins.

clue.text: This person's system of principles rejects English body of stories

parts.note: the speaker's own is my

indicators.note: rejects means the letter for English is thrown out

parts.note: a theology is a system of religious beliefs and principles

explanation.surface: A speaker's belief system turns down an English collection of tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Mythology is the collected traditional legends of a people, a body of stories.

clue.text: On reflection, Houses of Parliament associated with low energy

indicators.note: on reflection means the letters appear as in a mirror, backwards

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

explanation.surface: Seen in hindsight, Parliament is linked with a lack of vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' looks like an adjective with energy, but it is the cow's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph is informal for vigour, liveliness or power.

clue.text: One from France linked to some elements of higher mathematics?

definitions.text: One from France linked to some elements of higher mathematics?

parts.note: F is the international vehicle code for France

indicators.note: some elements means only a run of letters from the middle of the phrase is kept, the rest discarded

explanation.surface: A Frenchman associated with advanced mathematics is described.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines Pierre de Fermat, while F (France) joins ERMAT, the letters left inside 'higher mathematics' once its front and back are dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre de Fermat was a French mathematician, famous for his Last Theorem.

clue.text: Initially, 20% of estuary disappeared in the drink

indicators.note: initially points to the start of the ten-letter phrase, whose first fifth, given by 20% of, is two letters
disappeared tells us those opening letters are removed

parts.note: an estuary is a river mouth

explanation.surface: Part of an estuary vanished in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: RIVER MOUTH has ten letters, so the opening 20% is its first two; 'Initially' and 'disappeared' remove them.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermouth is a fortified wine flavoured with herbs, drunk as an aperitif.

clue.text: For example, a landlady

definitions.meaning: the character a is an example of an alphabetic symbol
a landlady lets out rooms, so she is one who lets

explanation.definitionFit: A is one of the alphabet's characters, and a landlady is someone who lets property.

clue.text: Perhaps, extremely bossy person at No 11 firing 14 after review

indicators.note: extremely means the extreme letters, first and last, of the word
firing means dismissing, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: the Chancellor of the Exchequer lives at 11 Downing Street

indicators.note: after review means that answer is read backwards before being removed

parts.note: 14 refers to the answer to 14 across, the word meaning register

explanation.surface: A domineering Chancellor sacks a staff member after an appraisal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after review' reverses the answer to 14 Across, giving LLOR, which 'firing' removes from the Chancellor, who lives at 11 Downing Street.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening by chance might or might not occur, so it means possibly or perhaps.
